newsitem.title: PERU: Peru and Shell/Mobil consortium sign oil contract.
newsitem.headline: Peru and Shell/Mobil consortium sign oil contract.

text.p: The Peruvian government and a consortium of oil firms including Royal Dutch/Shell and Mobil signed a contract Tuesday to explore and develop oil Block 75 in Peru's jungle.
Shell spokesman Andrew Vickers told Reuters the 30- to 40- year exploration and development accord was signed Tuesday by a representatives of the group and of Peru's oil contracting entity PeruPetro.

Vickers said the oil companies plan to invest up to $23 million over two years to drill one well and reprocess 186 miles (300 kms) of the 2,800-square-mile (7,900-square-km) block in the initial exploration phase.
"An environmental impact assessment and the consultation with an array of groups will precede any exploration on lot 75," Vickers said.

The oil block straddles the borders of Ucayali, Junin, Madre de Dios and Cuzco departments in central and southern Peru, adjacent to the massive Camisea gas fields also being developed by the Shell/Mobil group.
"Geographically it's very close to Camisea and from a geological point of view, the rock structures are similar," Vickers said, adding the block may yield natural gas as well as oil.
The block also will be developed in a fashion similar to Camisea, with as little disturbance as possible to the fragile surrounding lowland jungle environment, he said.
"It's like microsurgery," he said. "There will be no roads going to the well site. Everything will be shipped up the Amazon, put on barges and then flown in by helicopter."
Shell Prospecting and Development (Peru) B.V. and Mobil Exploration and Producing Peru Inc are the subsidiaries of the two oil giants that will carry out the exploration work in block 75.
For a contract signed last May, Shell and Mobil also formed a consortium to explore the huge oil gas reserves of the Camisea fields in the same region.
Camisea is Peru's largest hydrocarbon project, which is expected to last 40 years and become the largest foreign investment commitment in Peru at up to an estimated $3.0 billion.
PeruPetro now has 37 current oil contracts with private companies. Since it started offering the licenses four years ago, 15 have started producing oil, while 22 are at the exploration stage.

PeruPetro is negotiating five more exploration and development contracts with Coastal and Atlantic Richfield Company ; Argentina's Pluspetrol; Britain's Enterprise Oil ; and Peru's Buenaventura Ingenieros, according to the Energy and Mines ministry.
